Definition: to tend a flock; i.e. pasture it; in transitively, to graze (literally or figuratively); generally to rule; by extension, to associate with (as a friend)
BiblicalUsage: The LORD is my shepherd, says David, and Jacob blesses the God who fed him all his life long — the word there is shepherded. Ezekiel promises one shepherd over them, God's servant David, who shall feed them, and Micah asks God to feed his people with his rod, the flock of his heritage.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the LORD is my shepherd is the whole gospel in one line, and David knew it before he was king. I hold that God feeds his people the way a shepherd feeds his flock, and the one shepherd he promised is his servant David, the king who feeds.
